Synopsis:
    The US federal budget deficit for August 2026 came in at $167B, down 52% YoY, but primarily due to a calendar shift in Medicare/Social Security payments into July. Adjusted deficit was $248B, up $7B YoY. The fiscal year-to-date gap stands at $1.97T, already exceeding the full FY2025 deficit of $1.775T. Interest payments on federal debt fell $14B in August due to inflation accrual changes, but are up $143B (+13%) YTD. On the revenue side, customs receipts provided a net $12.84B inflow after $10.54B in tariff refunds — a marked improvement from July's $33.38B in refunds. YTD net customs inflows total $167.3B after $125.2B in refunds, following the Supreme Court's February ruling limiting tariff collection authority under IEEPA.

However, the signal is weak — this is not a rates-focused article.
